Subject: Initial questions on DPA, subprocessors and data flows

Hi Laura,

Thanks for the demo last week. Before we proceed to a procurement review, our security team has a few follow-ups around privacy and data handling. Can you confirm the following items?

1) A copy of the latest DPA and whether Redwood accepts the standard Acme Addendum (we can share our redlines if needed).
2) A list of subprocessors that will process Acme customer data (names, function, location, and whether they receive PII).
3) Data transfer controls: do you rely on SCCs, Binding Corporate Rules, or other transfer mechanisms for EU data?
4) A high-level data flow diagram showing where PII is stored, cached, and encrypted in the inference path (including logs, KV cache, telemetry).
5) Access controls and audit logging: which roles can view raw inputs/outputs, and how long audit logs are retained?

We need these to complete our security questionnaire. Appreciate a response by EOD Wed so we can keep the procurement timeline.

Best,
Daniel

Hi Daniel —

Thanks for the clear list. Quick summary below and attached items (redwood-dpa_v3.pdf, subprocessor-matrix.xlsx, pii-dataflow-diagram.svg). I'll paste concise answers and have Dev/Evelyn add technical details where needed.

1) DPA: We have attached redwood-dpa_v3.pdf. We are open to reviewing Acme redlines; we generally accept mutual DPA addenda but prefer to maintain our standard breach notification and liability caps.

2) Subprocessors: See attached subprocessor-matrix.xlsx for an exportable list. High level: cloud infra (GCP us-west1, storage & compute), managed metrics & logging (third-party APM vendor), payment processor (for billing only). Only the infrastructure and logging vendors touch encrypted tokens or telemetry; we mark which subprocessors touch PII in the matrix.

3) Data transfers: For EU-origin data we rely primarily on SCCs for hosted customers and offer EU-only deployments for customers who require EEA residency. For Private deployments we support customer KMS and on-prem options.

4) Data flow diagram: Attached (pii-dataflow-diagram.svg) — summary: customer request -> API ingress -> auth & routing -> serving runtime (in-memory KV cache; ephemeral, encrypted at rest if persisted for warm-start) -> model output returned. We do not persist raw PII to long-term storage by default; logs are redacted/hashed unless configured otherwise.

5) Access controls & logging: Role-based access via SSO (SCIM + RBAC). Only engineers with explicit privilege can view raw payloads; access requests generate ticketed approvals and are logged. Audit logs retained for 365 days by default; extended retention is an add-on.

Next steps: Dev will add the exact encryption (KMS) and key handling details, and Evelyn will confirm SOC2 controls and the procedure for ad-hoc data subject requests.

Subject: Re: Technical details: encryption, KV cache, and transient storage

Hi Daniel — quick technical addendum to Laura's note: 

- KV cache and runtime: The serving runtime keeps KV cache in memory for active sessions. For warm-start across instances we persist an encrypted checkpoint to ephemeral SSD. These checkpoints are encrypted using customer-specific keys when configured (Customer-managed KMS) or Redwood-managed KMS otherwise.
- Encryption: At-rest encryption for persisted artifacts uses AES-256; keys are wrapped with Google KMS (for hosted GCP deployments) or with customer KMS for Private/EU deployments.
- Logs & telemetry: Application logs have structured fields; any token-like fields are redacted by default. Full request/response logs are only stored if debug mode is enabled for troubleshooting and are time-limited (default 48 hours) unless the customer opts into extended retention.
- PII scope: We classify PII according to Acme's categories (identifiers, credentials, payment info, special categories). Our matrix indicates which subprocessors may process hashed identifiers vs. raw personal data.

I've updated the attached pii-dataflow-diagram.svg to label the exact encryption points and included a note about the KMS key policy. If you want, we can schedule a 30-min runthrough with infra to walk the flow for your security team.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Senior Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime

Daniel —

Thanks for the review. A couple of clarifications from security/controls perspective: 

- Audit logs: We retain immutable audit trails for admin actions for 365 days; API-level request traces are retained 90 days by default. We can provide compressed export for longer-term retention if Acme requires it for compliance.
- Data subject requests: We support a process to locate and purge customer-provided data; for hosted customers we can purge within 48 hours of a verified request. For Private deployments, the customer controls purge.
- Subprocessor onboarding: New subprocessors are evaluated via our vendor security program; we notify customers of material changes and publish an updated subprocessor list quarterly or upon request for contract-level customers.

Next steps I propose:
1) Laura/Procurement: review redwood-dpa_v3.pdf and provide any Acme redlines. If redlines are minor, we can accept and proceed to DocuSign.
2) Daniel/Security: if helpful, schedule a 30-minute tech call with Dev and me to walk the pii-dataflow-diagram and confirm encryption/KMS details.

I'm attaching the DPA again with an inline summary of clauses relevant to PII handling so your legal team can triage quickly. If you email Procurement with preferred signer info, I'll route the DocuSign link.

Best,
